title: Fix non-cone sparse baseline commands for omitted root inputs
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

A non-cone sparse checkout that omits a selected root input such as `LICENSE` cannot complete baseline setup: the preflight emits `git sparse-checkout add .`, but `.` is a literal non-cone pattern and leaves the input absent. Repeating the command leaves the same omission.

Generate materialization patterns in the checkout's existing mode. Cone-mode directory commands stay unchanged. Non-cone commands anchor and escape root files and package directories, restoring required inputs without matching similarly named paths. The preflight stays read-only. Sparse/HEAD validation, deletion and staged-drift rejection, batched path validation, schema routing and baseline authentication remain intact; configuration-read failures propagate before a command is published. This is a tooling repair; no new κ or selected-frontier change.

## Task and overlap

User-directed checking/process improvement; refined `portable-replay` suggestion, scope key `91a9a2afec282c926282`, chooser seed `6a5ebbaaab445e684ab18ccc01d0aa90`, priority revision 7. Concrete object: the emitted command for valid omitted root files in a non-cone checkout. Base/refreshed main: `32890bc5de034ab8fc93ac88ead7279a6a416d04`; contribution: `efd8edfcc20f8023a8832ba0efa1046143180261`.

Targeted all-state PR searches for sparse/materialize, non-cone and root-level baseline work found #3725, #4631 and #4936. This restores the next step their helper promises while retaining their validation contracts. Recent handoffs were consulted; #5463's Windows stream-reader work is separate. Coverage is limited, not an exhaustive novelty certificate: the offline overlap helper had no usable remote snapshot and incomplete local inventory. No mathematical predecessor executable was changed.

## Validation

All 16 sparse baseline regression tests pass on Python 3.12, normal and optimized, locally on Windows and in [hosted Linux/Windows checks](https://github.com/fluorine/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40171275529). The workflow lives separately on the contributor fork's main; its checkout is the contribution branch.

```sh
python -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_baseline_sparse*.py'
python -O -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_baseline_sparse*.py'
python -B scripts/research_selected_baseline.py
```

The new real-Git regression follows the emitted command, restores root LICENSE, a spaced/bracketed root filename and a spaced/bracketed package, reaches zero omissions, and keeps unrelated root files, wildcard decoys and nested same-name paths omitted. The old command's failure was reproduced before editing. An injected configuration failure is also rejected. Existing late-deletion, staged-drift and Git-failure controls remain.

Selected source/metadata verification passes locally and in [hosted Linux verification](https://github.com/fluorine/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40172161696), reporting `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY` for selected #5413, κ = `605457647/200000000000`. Native Windows required repository-local Git long-path support and restoring missing inputs after an initial path-length failure. This authenticates source/metadata only, not native operators, supplier admission or the complete theorem. `git diff --check` passes. No full selected cold replay, Lean, Docker or unrelated historical replay was run.

## Credit

Prepared for Joseph Anglada (@fluorine) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Retains Douglas Colkitt's helper, Arham-Tahir64's sparse contract and the explicit-inventory/Windows batching predecessor repairs. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

A separate review could bound the emitted materialization command itself on Windows; this repair does not add an executor or change sparse mode. Large directory-level fetches remain broader than an exact-file export. Neither question needs a scientific frontier change.
